A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HQ-DM work, and all supplied pages are readable. However, both reference an appendix that is absent from the files. V3 additionally refers to unavailable ablations, preventing confirmation of whether v1's Hadamard-order study and supplementary visualizations were relocated.

before.justification: V1 reports original LDM quantization results on ImageNet and LSUN, a Hadamard-order ablation, training-loss curves, and activation and generated-image analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original LDM and DiT evaluations, component ablations, weight-distribution diagnostics, and training-time and inference-latency measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains LoRA-based distillation, timestep-dependent quantization scales, symmetric activation quantization, and activation-only Hadamard transformations with inverse transformations before linear or convolution operations. DiT evaluation and the new ablation variants do not establish a change to HQ-DM itself.

E1.justification: ImageNet conditional generation and LSUN-Bedrooms/Churches unconditional generation remain. V3 Table 4 adds ImageNet generation at 512×512, extending the resolution requirement beyond v1's 256×256 evaluations. The additional DiT architecture is an experimental configuration change.

E2.justification: V3 adds QuEST to the LSUN-Bedrooms comparisons at W3A4 and W2A4, whereas v1 evaluated it only on ImageNet. V3 Table 6 also introduces DHQ-DM as a direct competing transformation scheme across four bit configurations, substantially strengthening comparison of the central design choice.

E3.justification: V3 introduces DiT-XL evaluation with the Improved DDPM sampler and 50 denoising steps, component controls involving fixed versus learnable scales, and quality/latency comparisons against DHQ-DM with single-Hadamard convolution layers. It also changes the weight diagnostic's layer and measurements. The existing LDM sampling counts and 50,000-image evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds component ablations separating Hadamard, LoRA, and scale-learning effects, plus direct single-versus-double transformation and efficiency analyses. Its Figure 4 replaces v1's projection-weight channel plots with attention-key weight statistics. V1's order sweep and Section 7 visual analyses are absent from the supplied v3; their possible relocation to the referenced appendix cannot be verified.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3's new kurtosis and outlier-ratio measurements characterize weight distributions rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: V3 adds DiT, component-ablation, DHQ-DM, and timing results. Existing values also change: Table 1 reports HQ-DM W4A8 IS/FID as 355.59/10.07 instead of 350.22/9.85, and EfficientDM W8A8 IS as 362.34 instead of 363.71. Table 2 changes TFMQ-DM W3A4/W2A4 FID from 25.74/25.77 to 227.64/245.85 without explaining the revisions. Previously blank baseline cells are populated; the headline W4A4/W4A3 HQ-DM results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion, quantization, LoRA/distillation, Hadamard, and linear/convolution derivations remain mathematically equivalent. Equations are combined or renumbered and a duplicate block-diagonal definition is removed, but no substantive formal result, proof, or correction is introduced.

C1.justification: V3 removes the introduction's explicit 'for the first time' priority assertion. The principal contributions otherwise remain: activation-outlier suppression, integer-convolution support, avoidance of additional weight outliers, and the same 12.8%/467.73% headline IS improvements.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets its component results as showing benefits independent of distillation adjustments and learnable LSQ scales. It extends applicability arguments beyond U-Net to Transformers and interprets comparable training times as evidence of negligible Hadamard overhead. These substantially expand the earlier interpretation, which focused on low-bit gains, weight stability, and Hadamard order.

D1.justification: V3 adds single-A100 hardware information and training/calibration costs, documents the DiT sampler, and explains the convolution fallback used in DHQ-DM. These improve documentation of the added experiments, but numerical learning rates, LoRA rank, and other referenced appendix details remain unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 adds foundational LoRA/QLoRA, DiT, and quantization/optimization references, classifies QuEST alongside QAT methods, and more explicitly acknowledges EfficientDM's distillation contribution. Broad generation and alternative-compression citations are pruned, while the central positioning against EfficientDM, QuaRot, and Xi et al. remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and background are tightened, contribution wording is softened, and experimental discussion gains separate LDM/DiT and component/transformation headings. The principal section order and most method exposition remain intact; much of the apparent document expansion comes from layout and added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 switches from two-column to single-column formatting, redraws the overview diagram, separates the transformation schematics from the revised weight diagnostic, and adds a timing panel and several tables. Existing tables are restructured, while v1's extensive supplementary plots and image grids are not included in the supplied v3.

improvement.justification: V1's ablation only varied Hadamard order; v3 Tables 5–6 directly test component contributions and the central single-versus-double transformation choice, including latency. Together with DiT evaluation, these address substantial gaps in validating the method and its applicability. These gains outweigh the unavailable order/visual analyses, although missing appendix details and unexplained large baseline-score revisions remain important transparency weaknesses.
